hard_cap_note: No default hard cap. Using a tool that an apron forbids hard-caps the team at that apron for the season (e.g. full NT-MLE → hard cap at the 1st apron). Triggers listed follow the forum's rule ('the exception the apron forbids') applied to each restriction — an approximation for the items the forum didn't spell out individually.

sections.title: Salary Cap & Cap Room
items: The salary cap for 2005 is $49,500,000.
Cap room = salary cap − team salary (cap salary, including cap holds and charges). A team with cap room can sign free agents or absorb salary up to the cap.

sections.title: How team salary is calculated
items: Player salaries on the books for the season (active contracts).
Cap holds (count toward the cap only — not the tax or the floor).
Incomplete roster charge (offseason only): one rookie-minimum salary for each player below 12 counted on the books.
Exception holds, while a team is under the cap.
For tax purposes, non-draft free agents earning below the 2-year veteran minimum are counted at the 2-year veteran minimum.
Second-round picks (Rookie Draft rules thread): guaranteed contracts count toward team salary at the index amounts; two-way contracts carry no salary cost.
Note: the forum post lists 8 components; the pasted summary names the ones above. See the forum's 'How Is Team Salary Calculated' post for the complete list.

sections.title: Over vs under the cap
items: By default every team operates as an over-the-cap team (exceptions available: Non-Taxpayer MLE and Bi-Annual Exception, subject to aprons).
Once a team uses its cap room it becomes an under-the-cap team for the season and cannot switch back; only the Room Exception ($2,811,000) remains.

sections.title: Luxury tax
items: Computed on team salary (tax salary) as of the final regular-season game; cap holds and exceptions are excluded.
Tax line: $60,143,000 ($10,643,000 above the cap).
Rates rise in $1,820,000 brackets (see table); every further bracket adds $0.50 per $1.
Repeater: a team that paid tax in at least 3 of the previous 4 seasons pays repeater rates.
About 50% of tax collected is split evenly among non-taxpaying teams; paid at season end.
Example: a non-repeater $5,000,000 over the tax pays $8,855,000.

sections.title: 1st apron ($62,709,000) restrictions
items: No acquiring players via sign-and-trade.
No Bi-Annual Exception.
No full Non-Taxpayer MLE (Taxpayer MLE only).
Cannot sign a waived player whose prior salary exceeded the Non-Taxpayer MLE.
Cannot use trade exceptions from a prior season.
Trades: incoming salary limited to 100% of outgoing (100% salary matching).
Apron restrictions take effect immediately.

sections.title: 2nd apron ($66,511,000) restrictions
items: All 1st-apron restrictions, plus:
No Taxpayer MLE.
No aggregating player salaries in trades.
No cash in trades.
Cannot send players out via sign-and-trade.
The team's 1st-round pick 7 years out is frozen (cannot be traded); it unfreezes if the team is below the 2nd apron in 3 of the next 4 seasons.
If the team is above the 2nd apron in 2 of the next 4 seasons, the frozen pick moves to the end of the 1st round.

sections.title: Hard-cap triggers
items: There is no hard cap by default.
Using an exception or tool that an apron forbids hard-caps the team at that apron for the season — e.g. using the full Non-Taxpayer MLE hard-caps the team at the 1st apron.

sections.title: Salary floor
items: Salary floor = 90% of the cap = $44,550,000.
Cap holds do not count toward the floor.
Any team below the floor when offseason free agency ends will have players auto-signed to reach the floor, and players may be cut as needed to make room.

stepien.label: ASSUMED (standard NBA Stepien rule): a team can't be left without a 1st-round pick in consecutive future drafts.

league_cash.label: League cash
league_cash.note: League cash is a separate in-league currency outside the salary cap: it never counts as salary for matching, payroll, tax or aprons. Team balances aren't on the stats site — enter them manually.
league_cash.max_per_trade_note: League rule: Taxpayer MLE rounded DOWN to the nearest $1M (app computes it from exceptions.taxpayer_mle: $1,820,000 → $1,000,000). Exceeding it fails the trade.
